definition: The optional handle a consumer holds to return every expanded fold in a viewer to folded; the viewer keeps the fold state itself.
The single row standing in for a run of folded unchanged lines, reading "Expand N lines ..." unless the consumer supplies its content.
One row of a line diff: an optional old line and an optional new line with their change kind, as either view reads it.
A removed line paired in order with the added line immediately following it, shown as one change rather than a removal and an addition.
A token removed from or added to a modified line, marked within that line under the selected compare method.
The compact chip showing a line's terminator as escaped text (`\n`, `\r\n`, `\r`) on each side of a line ending change.
A difference only in leading or trailing whitespace between a modified pair's lines, marked under trimmed line comparison.
The compact chip reading `WS` on each side's line of a pair carrying a whitespace change.
A line's side and number joined by a hyphen, `L` for old and `R` for new, as in `L-20`.
A stable `dxdiff`-prefixed class naming an element's kind, view, or state, which apps and themes style against.
The class-name prefix on every styling hook, keeping the viewer's classes from colliding with an app's own.
